items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: That's right; of course, she catered to all, Jack Legs Diamond and [...] everybody, all them racketeers, cost you $50.00 to say hello. That's right, that's no exaggeration, and it was my friend and they liked us

ctx.x: Tell me this, when you first -- how did you feel when you all first went into the Cotton Club?

I hated it. I left all that money, man down there during Prohibition, I done left all -- I had a good thing. I had the horseshoe in my hand, baby. When I went to the Cotton Club, they put pressure on. They put pressure on us, and no denying at that time when the Syndicate say they want something, they got it or you wasn't in the business, so we had to go along with the program.

But I hate it, I would never like it. I had a good name, right in Harlem, New York, I had it made. I was making good money and I had my hustle, me and the piano player going around the tables. I had my hustle -- I had my friends, if and say, "Sonny, you and Duke come on over." Pollyanna and everybody, you heard of My boon coop! Pollyanna? / "Come on over," Go over there and interchange for about an hour or so, give Duke a hundred, give me a hundred. That was a lot of money then.
